_meta.purpose: AUTHORITATIVE NCAA D1 league averages + standard deviations + WAR constants for 2026, recomputed on the CORRECTED (post-CSV-fix) Master data. Each value carries a 'why it matters'.
_meta.source: docs/drs-reference/Full Season {Hitting,Pitching} Master Stats.csv (quote-aware) filtered to Hitter/Pitching Master division=D1
_meta.weighting: MEANS = aggregate Σnum/Σden over ALL D1 (PA/IP-weighted). SDs = per-player POPULATION SD on the QUALIFIED subset (PA>=100 n=3019 / IP>=30 n=1988) so tiny-sample noise doesn't inflate spread. NOTE the qualified-subset mean differs slightly from the all-D1 aggregate (qualified players are better): use the aggregate mean to CENTER value, the qualified SD to measure SPREAD/z-scores — and keep the normalization population consistent wherever a '+'-stat is built.

lgwOBA.why: THE hitter anchor. Centers wRAA (value=0 at league avg) AND is the wRC+ denom. Every hitter WAR rides on it. SD 0.0526 = spread of hitter quality on the wOBA scale. POPULATION MATTERS: qualified regulars (PA>=100) average 0.3874 — do NOT anchor there, it would drop every hitter ~0.19 WAR vs descriptive (which centers all-D1). The 0.3782-vs-0.3874 difference is a population choice, not an error.

wOBAscale.derivation: = lgOBP / lg_raw (league raw wOBA above-out per PA), from scripts/drs/derive_woba_weights.py. <1 (vs MLB's 1.15-1.25) because D1's higher run environment makes one wOBA point worth MORE runs: 1/0.947 = 1.06 runs/PA per wOBA unit vs MLB ~0.80. Validated by RESULT: RUNS_PER_PA = lgwOBA/wOBAscale = 0.3994 reproduces descriptive wRAA at 0.04 WAR error.
wOBAscale.why: Converts wOBA points -> runs (wRAA=(wOBA-lgwOBA)/wOBAscale*PA). Sets oWAR RUNS_PER_PA. wRAA is scale-independent so descriptive is unaffected by small changes; self-consistent pair with lgwOBA.

lgOBP.why: On-base component. Dominant wRC+ term (coef 0.691) — captures the walk, the single most under-priced skill vs MLB. Reference for OBP+ / conference scaling.

lgSLG.why: Slugging component (wRC+ coef 0.235). Carries ALL power (ISO redundant once SLG is in). SD 0.106 = widest slash spread -> power is where hitters most differentiate.

lgAVG.why: Batting average. Display + small-sample blend; NOT in wRC+ (redundant vs OBP/SLG).

lgISO.why: Isolated power (SLG-AVG). Display + power ratings; redundant for wRC+ (power already in SLG).

lgERA.why: Earned-run environment. Anchors ERA+ and, with lgRA9, defines E2T. IP-weighted.

lgRA9.why: TOTAL-run environment (the WAR currency). Anchors RPW and replacement level. Everything pitcher-WAR is measured against this, not ERA.

E2T.why: Earned->Total bridge (=lgRA9/lgERA=ΣR/ΣER). FIP is on an EARNED scale; WAR needs TOTAL runs, so projFIP*E2T -> projRA9. Without it pitcher WAR is ~14% too generous.

lgK9.why: Strikeout rate. FIP input (coef -0.231) + the most PERSISTENT skill (r=0.578) -> carries repeatability. SD 2.144 is the K9+ denominator.

lgBB9.why: Walk rate. FIP input (coef 0.509 w/ HBP). The D1 walk is repriced FAR above MLB — the signature derive-don't-borrow finding. SD 1.571 = BB9+ denom; long right tail (wildness, maxZ 5.7).

lgHR9.why: Home-run rate. FIP input (coef 1.486, the heaviest). Sits in the LUCK bucket -> the GB%-informed HR9 refinement (Step 4) reclaims groundballer skill here.

lgHBP9.why: Hit-by-pitch rate. Folded INTO the walk term (BB9+HBP9). JUSTIFIED by OUR RE24 run values: BB 0.458 vs HBP 0.478 — near-identical D1 run cost, so one coefficient is correct. This is a D1 derivation, NOT a copy of MLB FIP (which also groups them but at a different absolute ratio). Not a free predictor (over-fits HBP > walk).

RPW.why: Runs-per-win: the denominator that turns runs into WAR. Derived from lgRA9 6.915 (Pythagorean 2R), locked. BOTH sides share it or the desc-vs-proj gap is a fake scale artifact.

replacement_RA9.why: Pitcher ZERO point of WAR (win%-anchor .380, DERIVED not a mean). A pitcher AT 8.83 RA9 = 0 WAR; the gap (8.83 - his RA9) x IP is his value.

hitter_replacement_wins_per_600pa.why: Hitter zero point (BORROWED convention). A league-avg 600-PA hitter = 2.0 oWAR, replacement = 0. RE-DERIVE both sides on one tier principle at Step 5; the hitter/pitcher SPLIT is the output.

oWAR_RUNS_PER_PA.why: =lgwOBA/wOBAscale = lg_raw (league-avg raw wOBA-above-out per PA over ALL D1). Converts a wRC+ deviation -> runs so projection oWAR reproduces descriptive wRAA. CONFIRMED from THREE independent angles (scripts/drs/_recenter_check.mjs): pure-RE24 == wOBA-method == wRC+xRPP all collapse to one number once the linear-weights out-weight is centered on all-D1 (-0.3994). REPLACES the wrong 0.163 (=ΣR/ΣPA, absolute run rate, a DIFFERENT quantity that compressed elite bats ~2x). ARCHITECTURE: READ FROM THIS FIXTURE with a runtime stale-guard, NOT inline (2nd constant-drift bug after 0.364). Inline sites to replace: war.ts:14, edge index.ts:903, TB re-inlines.
oWAR_RUNS_PER_PA.segmented_residual_2026_08_10: projection oWAR vs descriptive, grand |err| 0.054; FLAT across wRC+/PA/BB% except (1) top-19 bats wRC+>=140 +0.09 (irreducible slash-proxy 2B/3B/HR split), (2) systematic -0.016->-0.029 signed = descriptive still on POOL lgwOBA 0.3774; closes when Step-6 re-populate uses all-D1 0.3782.

hitter_wRCplus.why: Display index of hitter offense; anchored on lgwOBA 0.3782 (NOT 0.3667, the intercept-less proxy mean). SD ~14 ≈ MLB's ~15 (sane). Feeds oWAR via RUNS_PER_PA. Validated: OLS wOBA~OBP+SLG corr 0.9958 on corrected data.
hitter_wRCplus.denom_note: Anchor = the true NCAA average wOBA over all D1 (0.3782). Coeffs 0.691/0.235 (validated, corr 0.996). That's it — 0.3667 (intercept-less proxy) and 0.3874 (qualified-regulars subset) are NOT the league average.
hitter_wRCplus.index_is_a_ratio_not_a_run_currency: wRC+ is a wOBA-RATIO; D1-FIP is a RUN-ESTIMATE. Different constructions, so 'a 160 hitter == a 160 pitcher' is false — compare WAR, not indices.

pitcher_D1FIP.why: Pitcher quality on a RUN scale (mean 5.514 ≈ lgERA). Validated: same-season |proj_pwar-desc_pwar| 0.297≈0.30 (vs old pRV+ blend 0.59).
pitcher_D1FIP.tail_note: CRITICAL: D1-FIP's top tail is SHORT (best pitcher only 2.54 SD below mean) but desc_pWAR's tail is LONG (maxZ 4.86) — the IP-leverage in (repl-FIP*E2T)*IP/9/RPW restores the value tail. FIP is a RUN estimate, NOT a z-index, so its SD does NOT govern WAR. Do NOT z-normalize or SD-stretch it — that is exactly the mistake the old pRV+ made (z-averaging compressed its tail to 3.1 SD and buried aces). The run-mapping, not the spread, is the calibration.
